prompt:
Style: a walk-cycle sprite sheet for a 2D narrative role-playing game whose art is expressive oil painting. The figure is painted, not drawn: thick impasto with clearly visible, broad directional brushstrokes, built from a few large planes of bold colour, no line art, no cartoon outlines, no cel shading. The strokes must stay broad and few so that the figure still reads at a small size on screen. Lighting like the attached portrait: warm cadmium-orange light from the right, cool ultramarine and violet shadows on the left side, reflected teal light in the dark fur. Use the first attached reference image only for the character design (costume, clothes colours, body proportions); use the second attached image, an oil-painted portrait of the same character, for the painting technique, brushwork and palette. Avoid: smooth digital gradients, photorealism, a cute cartoon look, a 3D-render look.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Sheet layout: the badger courier in strict side view (profile) walking to the right. One row of 6 animation frames of a walk cycle, evenly spaced, same scale, feet on the same baseline, the whole figure fully visible in every frame with empty space between the frames. Phases: contact (front foot forward), down, passing (legs together), up, contact with the other foot forward, down. The parcel stays under the arm nearer to the viewer; the scarf ends swing slightly behind. Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Style: a sheet of separate visual-effect elements for a 2D game whose art is expressive oil painting. Every element is painted with thick impasto oil paint: clearly visible bristle marks, loaded single strokes and palette-knife dabs, bold colour, no line art, no smooth digital gradients, no airbrush.

Elements, arranged in a clear grid of three rows with generous empty space around each element, nothing touching or overlapping:
Row 1: a seagull in flight seen from the side, flying to the right, painted with a few quick strokes of white and pale grey with dark grey wingtips, shown three times in three wing positions: wings raised high, wings level, wings lowered.
Row 2: four separate soft puffs of chimney smoke, each a cluster of round-brush strokes in grey-violet and blue-grey with warm orange light on one edge, of slightly different shapes.
Row 3: four short horizontal glints of light on water, each one or two loaded palette-knife strokes of cadmium orange, lemon yellow and pale cream; and one long tapered ray of pale yellow light, a wide dry-brush stroke that fades out towards its far end, lying horizontally.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no frame borders, no labels.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: square 1:1.
